correctness.rationale: The original fixed-a, kappa>0 system has the exact invariant H=g(x)^2 y^2/2+int_0^x u g(u)^2 du; q=int_0^x g du is a global increasing diffeomorphism, and p=gy yields dot q=p, dot p=-W′(q) in physical time. The coercive single-well W has exactly two turning points, one minimal oval period at every E>0. At both signed infinities q~g/(kappa x-a), V~g²/(2kappa), so W(q)~q²log|q| and W′(q)~2qlog|q|. Exact W″(q)=1+x(kappa x-a)=O(log(2+|q|)) yields locally uniform and equi-Lipschitz scaled force F_E(z)=W′(Q_Ez)/(Q_E logE)->z; positive-turn initial z_E->1 and z′_E=0. Continuous dependence gives (z,z′)->(cos tau,-sin tau), with unique-monotone turn/crossing structure excluding spurious shorter returns; sqrt(log E)T(E)->2pi. The tail turning-coordinate equation yields x_±=a/kappa ±sqrt(logE/kappa)+o(1), and inverse q forces x/R_E->sgn cos(2pi s) except at the two transition phases, uniformly bounded by turning values; dominated convergence proves finite Lp and the two-atom occupation law. An independently implemented symbolic check verified H cancellation, canonical dp/dt and W″; independent high-precision quadrature at a=0,kappa=1 and A=3,5,8,10,14 shows normalized periods tending toward one, not proof of the universal limit.
